football_evidence.question: Can Charlotte contain Tulane’s explosive runs?
football_evidence.assessment: EdgeDesk’s number is 3.5 points closer to Tulane than the line, and EdgeDesk cannot account for most of that: its own breakdown accounts for about 0.0 of the 3.5 points. The measured football evidence leans toward Charlotte, not toward EdgeDesk’s number. Treat the gap as an open research question, not as an edge.
supporting: When Charlotte has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Charlotte’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 22.7% of its runs, and Tulane’s defense stops 13.6% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.5%).

When Tulane has the ball (big plays on the ground): Tulane’s offense turns 8.1% of its runs into explosive gains, and Charlotte’s defense gives up explosive gains on 8.8% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).
In his last two games (Louisiana and Memphis), Gonzales averaged 4.6 yards per attempt, against 7.6 in his three games before that.
EdgeDesk’s position-group ratings put Tulane’s offensive line No. 61 nationally and Charlotte’s No. 138.
contradicting: When Tulane has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Tulane’s offense has allowed a sack on 7.9% of its dropbacks, and Charlotte’s defense sacks the quarterback on 5.3% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).

When Tulane has the ball (big plays through the air): Tulane’s offense turns 7.9% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Charlotte’s defense gives up explosive gains on 13.3% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.2%).
In his last two games (North Texas and Temple), Harrell averaged 9.4 yards per attempt, against 4.9 in his two games before that.
In his last two games (Southern Miss and Army), Semonza averaged 5.8 yards per attempt, against 7.5 in his three games before that.
quarterbacks: Cole Gonzales has completed 77 of 125 passes (61.6%) for 863 yards, 6.9 yards per attempt, 3 touchdowns and 7 interceptions in five games for Charlotte, and has been sacked on 5 of 130 dropbacks.
Conner Harrell has completed 51 of 72 passes (70.8%) for 592 yards, 8.2 yards per attempt, 3 touchdowns and 2 interceptions in four games for Charlotte, and has been sacked on 5 of 77 dropbacks.
Kadin Semonza has completed 64 of 119 passes (53.8%) for 808 yards, 6.8 yards per attempt, 4 touchdowns and 2 interceptions in five games for Tulane, and has been sacked on 13 of 132 dropbacks.
Trace Johnson has completed 35 of 68 passes (51.5%) for 452 yards, 6.6 yards per attempt, 1 touchdown and 3 interceptions in three games for Tulane, and has been sacked on 4 of 72 dropbacks.
